revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Flooring
revealWordProblem.text:
A garden designer wants to cover a gazebo floor with tiles. The gazebo floor is a regular decagon with equal sides, shown here with a side of 3¾ feet and a distance of 5¾ feet from the center to the middle of a side.
Question: If floor tiles cost $2.89 per square foot, what budget do you recommend the designer have for the tiles?
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: A regular decagon gazebo floor labeled 3 and three-fourths feet on one side and 5 and three-fourths feet from the center to the middle of a side.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Decompose the decagon into 10 identical triangles that meet at the center. Each triangle has a base of 3¾ = 3.75 feet and a height of 5¾ = 5.75 feet, so its area is ½ × 3.75 × 5.75 = 10.78125 square feet. Ten triangles give 107.8125 square feet. At $2.89 per square foot, the tile cost is 107.8125 × 2.89 ≈ $311.58. I would recommend a budget of about $320 so there is room for a few extra tiles for cuts and breakage.

questions.stem: An L-shaped room is made of two rectangles: 10 ft × 6 ft and 4 ft × 3 ft. What is the total area?
questions.explanation: Area 1 = 10 × 6 = 60 sq ft. Area 2 = 4 × 3 = 12 sq ft. Total = 60 + 12 = 72 sq ft.
choiceFeedback: Double one side: area doubles.
Double both sides: area × 4.
hints: The L-shape is already split into two rectangles for you: 10 × 6 and 4 × 3.
Find each rectangle's area separately with A = l × w, then combine — joined shapes mean adding.
Compute 10 × 6 and 4 × 3, then add the two results. Label your answer in sq ft.
questions.stemEs: Una habitación en forma de L está formada por dos rectángulos: 10 ft × 6 ft y 4 ft × 3 ft. ¿Cuál es el área total?
questions.explanationEs: Área 1 = 10 × 6 = 60 sq ft. Área 2 = 4 × 3 = 12 sq ft. Total = 60 + 12 = 72 sq ft.
hintsEs: La figura en L ya está dividida en dos rectángulos por ti: 10 × 6 y 4 × 3.
Halla el área de cada rectángulo por separado con A = l × a y luego combínalas: figuras unidas significan sumar.
Calcula 10 × 6 y 4 × 3, y luego suma los dos resultados. Etiqueta tu respuesta en pies².

questions.stem: A rectangular patio is 15 ft × 10 ft with a 5 ft × 4 ft rectangular flower bed cut out. What is the remaining area?
questions.explanation: Patio = 15 × 10 = 150 sq ft. Cutout = 5 × 4 = 20 sq ft. Remaining = 150 − 20 = 130 sq ft.
choiceFeedback: Test: same perimeter, different areas?
A thin rectangle and a square can differ.
Perimeter does not determine area.
hints: The flower bed is CUT OUT of the patio — that phrase tells you which operation to use.
Find the full patio area (15 × 10) and the cutout area (5 × 4), then remove the cutout.
Compute 15 × 10 and 5 × 4, then subtract the flower bed's area from the patio's area.
questions.stemEs: Un patio rectangular mide 15 ft × 10 ft y tiene recortado un jardín rectangular de 5 ft × 4 ft. ¿Cuál es el área restante?
questions.explanationEs: Patio = 15 × 10 = 150 sq ft. Recorte = 5 × 4 = 20 sq ft. Área restante = 150 − 20 = 130 sq ft.
hintsEs: El jardín está RECORTADO del patio: esa frase te dice qué operación usar.
Halla el área total del patio (15 × 10) y el área del recorte (5 × 4), y luego quita el recorte.
Calcula 15 × 10 y 5 × 4, y luego resta el área del jardín del área del patio.

questions.stem: Find the area of an L-shape made of a 5×3 rectangle and a 2×4 rectangle.
choiceFeedback: Area and perimeter are not linked.
A thin shape can have big perimeter, small area.
You must use both to describe a shape.
hints: Two rectangles make this L: one is 5 × 3 and the other is 2 × 4.
Joined pieces mean you add their areas after computing each one with length × width.
Find 5 × 3, then 2 × 4, and add the two products together.
questions.stemEs: Halla el área de una figura en forma de L formada por un rectángulo de 5×3 y uno de 2×4.
hintsEs: Dos rectángulos forman esta L: uno es 5 × 3 y el otro es 2 × 4.
Las piezas unidas significan que sumas sus áreas después de calcular cada una con largo × ancho.
Halla 5 × 3, luego 2 × 4, y suma los dos productos.

reviewHighlights.watchOut: A common mistake in Area of Composite Figures is adding every piece even when a piece has been cut out of the figure. For a 10 ft by 8 ft rectangle with a 3 ft by 2 ft rectangular notch cut from one corner, students compute the full rectangle 10 × 8 = 80 sq ft and stop, or they add the notch instead of removing it (80 + 6 = 86 sq ft) instead of subtracting it: 80 − (3 × 2) = 80 − 6 = 74 sq ft. Before submitting, check whether each piece is part of the figure (add it) or missing from the figure (subtract it).

level1.stem: When should you subtract areas instead of adding them to find the area of a composite figure?
choices: When a piece is cut out or removed from a larger shape
When one shape is larger than the other
level1.explanation: Subtract when a piece is removed from a larger shape (like a window cut from a wall). Add when two shapes are joined together (like an L-shape).
choiceFeedback: Overlap is different — subtracting is for a piece removed.
Size alone doesn't decide — subtract only when part is removed.
Not always — you add pieces that are joined together.
hints: Think of real examples: a window in a wall versus two rooms joined into an L-shape.
Ask for each choice: is material missing from the shape, or are pieces being combined?
Picture a wall with a window: you can't paint the glass, so its area comes OFF the wall's area. Match that idea to a choice.
level1.stemEs: ¿Cuándo debes restar áreas en lugar de sumarlas para hallar el área de una figura compuesta?
level1.explanationEs: Resta cuando se quita una pieza de una figura más grande (como una ventana recortada en una pared). Suma cuando dos figuras se unen (como una figura en forma de L).
choicesEs: Cuando se corta o se quita una parte de una figura más grande

Siempre se resta — nunca se suma
hintsEs: Piensa en ejemplos reales: una ventana en una pared frente a dos cuartos unidos en forma de L.
Pregunta en cada opción: ¿le falta material a la figura o se están combinando piezas?
Imagina una pared con una ventana: no puedes pintar el vidrio, así que su área se QUITA del área de la pared. Une esa idea con una opción.

level1.stem: (Lesson 5.9) A regular hexagon is divided into 6 equal triangles from the center. Each triangle has a base of 6 ft and a height of 5.2 ft. What is the area of one triangle?
level1.explanation: A = ½ × b × h = ½ × 6 × 5.2 = 15.6 square feet.
choiceFeedback: 31.2 is 6 × 5.2 — the full rectangle. One triangle is half of that: multiply by ½.
11.2 comes from adding 6 + 5.2. Area means multiply base × height, then take half.
The number is right, but ft measures length. Area needs square units (sq ft).
hints: Focus on just ONE of the 6 triangles: its base is 6 ft and its height is 5.2 ft.
One triangle uses A = ½ × b × h — don't multiply by 6 yet; that step is for the whole hexagon.
Compute ½ × 6 × 5.2: take half of 6 first, then multiply by 5.2. Label it in sq ft.
level1.stemEs: Un hexágono regular se divide en 6 triángulos iguales desde el centro. Cada triángulo tiene una base de 6 ft y una altura de 5.2 ft. ¿Cuál es el área de un triángulo?
level1.explanationEs: A = ½ × b × h = ½ × 6 × 5.2 = 15.6 pies cuadrados.
hintsEs: Concéntrate en solo UNO de los 6 triángulos: su base es de 6 pies y su altura de 5.2 pies.
Un triángulo usa A = ½ × b × h; todavía no multipliques por 6, ese paso es para el hexágono completo.
Calcula ½ × 6 × 5.2: saca primero la mitad de 6 y luego multiplica por 5.2. Etiquétalo en pies².

level1.stem: (Lesson 5.9) Using the triangle from the previous question, what is the total area of the hexagonal skylight?
level1.explanation: Total area = 6 triangles × 15.6 sq ft = 93.6 square feet.
choiceFeedback: That is the area of ONE of the congruent triangles. The hexagon is made of 6 of them — how many triangle areas do you still need to add?
You multiplied by 12 instead of 6. Count the congruent triangles the hexagon decomposes into before you multiply.
That is 4 triangles, not 6. Re-count how many congruent triangles the hexagon breaks into.
hints: You already found one triangle's area (15.6 sq ft) in the last question — now think about the whole hexagon.
A regular hexagon splits into 6 identical triangles, so the total is 6 copies of one triangle's area.
Multiply 15.6 × 6. (Tip: do 15 × 6, then 0.6 × 6, and combine.)
level1.stemEs: Usando el triángulo de la pregunta anterior, ¿cuál es el área total del tragaluz hexagonal?

Multiplica 15.6 × 6. (Consejo: haz 15 × 6, luego 0.6 × 6 y combina.)

level2.stem: A 7 ft by 5 ft rectangle has a triangle (base 7 ft, height 4 ft) on top. Add the two areas. What is the total area?
level2.explanation: Rectangle = 7 x 5 = 35 sq ft. Triangle = 1/2 x 7 x 4 = 14 sq ft. The pieces are joined, so add: 35 + 14 = 49 sq ft.
choiceFeedback: Scale one dimension: area scales by that factor.
Scale both: area scales by the product.
Try: if both double, area goes × 4.
level2.stemEs: Un rectángulo de 7 ft por 5 ft tiene un triángulo (base 7 ft, altura 4 ft) encima. Suma las dos áreas. ¿Cuál es el área total?
level2.explanationEs: Rectángulo = 7 x 5 = 35 sq ft. Triángulo = 1/2 x 7 x 4 = 14 sq ft. Las piezas están unidas, así que suma: 35 + 14 = 49 sq ft.
hints: A composite figure is built from basic shapes, so measure each shape before you think about the total.
The rectangle uses length × width and the triangle uses ½ × base × height. The pieces are joined, so their areas combine.
Rectangle: 7 × 5 = 35 sq ft. Now find the triangle with ½ × 7 × 4 and combine the two areas.

El rectángulo usa largo × ancho y el triángulo usa ½ × base × altura. Las piezas están unidas, así que sus áreas se combinan.
Rectángulo: 7 × 5 = 35 sq ft. Ahora halla el triángulo con ½ × 7 × 4 y combina las dos áreas.

level2.stem: Plan 2 — L-shaped lobby: decompose the L into two rectangles, one 9 ft by 6 ft and one 7 ft by 3 ft, then ADD. What is the total floor area?
level2.explanation: First rectangle = 9 x 6 = 54 sq ft. Second rectangle = 7 x 3 = 21 sq ft. Joined L-shape, so add: 54 + 21 = 75 sq ft.
choiceFeedback: Can two shapes with same perimeter have different areas?
Yes—test with examples.
Perimeter and area are independent.
level2.stemEs: Plan 2 — Vestíbulo en forma de L: descompón la L en dos rectángulos, uno de 9 ft por 6 ft y otro de 7 ft por 3 ft, y luego SUMA. ¿Cuál es el área total del piso?
level2.explanationEs: Primer rectángulo = 9 x 6 = 54 sq ft. Segundo rectángulo = 7 x 3 = 21 sq ft. Es una L unida, así que suma: 54 + 21 = 75 sq ft.
hints: Decomposing means cutting the L into shapes you already know how to measure.
Find each rectangle's area with length × width, and note that the two pieces sit beside each other instead of overlapping.
First rectangle: 9 × 6 = 54 sq ft. Now find the second rectangle's area and combine it with the first.
hintsEs: Descomponer significa cortar la L en formas que ya sabes medir.
Halla el área de cada rectángulo con largo × ancho, y observa que las dos piezas están una al lado de la otra, sin traslaparse.
Primer rectángulo: 9 × 6 = 54 sq ft. Ahora halla el área del segundo rectángulo y combínala con la primera.

level2.stem: Plan 4 — Design studio: the floor is a 16 ft by 12 ft rectangle, but a 5 ft by 4 ft storage closet is cut out of one corner. Find the usable floor area.
level2.explanation: Large rectangle = 16 x 12 = 192 sq ft. Cutout closet = 5 x 4 = 20 sq ft. A piece is removed, so subtract: 192 - 20 = 172 sq ft.
choiceFeedback: That's the full floor — subtract the closet that's cut out.
You added the closet — it's removed, so subtract its area.
20 is just the closet — subtract it from the whole floor.
level2.stemEs: Plan 4 — Estudio de diseño: el piso es un rectángulo de 16 ft por 12 ft, pero se recorta un clóset de almacenamiento de 5 ft por 4 ft en una esquina. Halla el área útil del piso.
level2.explanationEs: Rectángulo grande = 16 x 12 = 192 sq ft. Clóset recortado = 5 x 4 = 20 sq ft. Se quita una pieza, así que resta: 192 - 20 = 172 sq ft.
hints: The closet is removed from the floor, so that corner is not usable space.
Find the area of the whole rectangle first, then the area of the cutout, and decide which operation takes one away from the other.
Whole floor: 16 × 12 = 192 sq ft. The closet covers 5 × 4 sq ft — take that piece away to finish.
hintsEs: El clóset se quita del piso, así que esa esquina no es espacio útil.
Halla primero el área del rectángulo completo, luego el área del recorte, y decide qué operación quita una de la otra.
Piso completo: 16 × 12 = 192 sq ft. El clóset cubre 5 × 4 sq ft: quita esa pieza para terminar.

level2.prompt: A T-shaped room can be decomposed in two different ways. Show both ways and prove they give the same total area. Use a T-shape where the top is 14 ft × 4 ft and the stem is 6 ft × 10 ft.
level2.sentenceFrame: Way 1: I split it into ___ and ___. Areas: ___ + ___ = ___. Way 2: I used a ___ rectangle and subtracted ___. Areas: ___ − ___ = ___. Both give ___ sq ft.
level2.hint: Write original area formula and scaled formula; compare.
hints: The T's top slab is 14 × 4 and its stem is 6 × 10. Way 1 simply adds those two rectangles.
For Way 2, wrap the whole T in one big rectangle and subtract the empty corner rectangles.
Way 1: 14 × 4 plus 6 × 10. Then build the big rectangle for Way 2 and show the subtraction lands on the same total.
level2.explanation: Way 1 splits the T into its two named rectangles: 14 × 4 = 56 plus 6 × 10 = 60, a total of 116 sq ft. Way 2 wraps the T in a 14 ft × 14 ft rectangle worth 196 sq ft and subtracts the two empty 4 ft × 10 ft corners, 196 − 80 = 116 sq ft — the same region is being measured, so the decomposition you choose cannot change the area.
level2.explanationEs: La Manera 1 divide la T en sus dos rectángulos nombrados: 14 × 4 = 56 más 6 × 10 = 60, un total de 116 sq ft. La Manera 2 envuelve la T en un rectángulo de 14 ft × 14 ft que vale 196 sq ft y resta las dos esquinas vacías de 4 ft × 10 ft, 196 − 80 = 116 sq ft: se está midiendo la misma región, así que la forma en que la descompongas no puede cambiar el área.
level2.promptEs: Un cuarto en forma de T se puede descomponer de dos maneras diferentes. Muestra las dos maneras y demuestra que dan la misma área total. Usa una forma de T donde la parte de arriba mida 14 pies × 4 pies y el tronco mida 6 pies × 10 pies.
hintsEs: La parte de arriba de la T es 14 × 4 y su tallo es 6 × 10. La Vía 1 simplemente suma esos dos rectángulos.
Para la Vía 2, envuelve toda la T en un rectángulo grande y resta los rectángulos vacíos de las esquinas.
Vía 1: 14 × 4 más 6 × 10. Luego arma el rectángulo grande de la Vía 2 y muestra que la resta llega al mismo total.

level3.explanationEs: La Manera 1 divide la T en sus dos rectángulos nombrados: 14 × 4 = 56 más 6 × 10 = 60, un total de 116 sq ft. La Manera 2 envuelve la T en un rectángulo de 14 ft × 14 ft que vale 196 sq ft y resta las dos esquinas vacías de 4 ft × 10 ft, 196 − 80 = 116 sq ft: se está midiendo la misma región, así que la forma en que la descompongas no puede cambiar el área.
level3.promptEs: Un cuarto en forma de T se puede descomponer de dos maneras diferentes. Muestra las dos maneras y demuestra que dan la misma área total. Usa una forma de T donde la parte de arriba mida 14 pies × 4 pies y el tronco mida 6 pies × 10 pies.
hintsEs: La parte de arriba de la T es 14 × 4 y su tallo es 6 × 10. La Vía 1 simplemente suma esos dos rectángulos.
Para la Vía 2, envuelve toda la T en un rectángulo grande y resta los rectángulos vacíos de las esquinas.
Vía 1: 14 × 4 más 6 × 10. Luego arma el rectángulo grande de la Vía 2 y muestra que la resta llega al mismo total.

level3.stem: Plan 2 — L-shaped lobby: decompose the L into two rectangles, one 9 ft by 6 ft and one 7 ft by 3 ft, then ADD. What is the total floor area?
level3.explanation: First rectangle = 9 x 6 = 54 sq ft. Second rectangle = 7 x 3 = 21 sq ft. Joined L-shape, so add: 54 + 21 = 75 sq ft.
choiceFeedback: Can two shapes with same perimeter have different areas?
Yes—test with examples.
Perimeter and area are independent.
level3.stemEs: Plan 2 — Vestíbulo en forma de L: descompón la L en dos rectángulos, uno de 9 ft por 6 ft y otro de 7 ft por 3 ft, y luego SUMA. ¿Cuál es el área total del piso?
level3.explanationEs: Primer rectángulo = 9 x 6 = 54 sq ft. Segundo rectángulo = 7 x 3 = 21 sq ft. Es una L unida, así que suma: 54 + 21 = 75 sq ft.
hints: Decomposing means cutting the L into shapes you already know how to measure.
Find each rectangle's area with length × width, and note that the two pieces sit beside each other instead of overlapping.
First rectangle: 9 × 6 = 54 sq ft. Now find the second rectangle's area and combine it with the first.
hintsEs: Descomponer significa cortar la L en formas que ya sabes medir.
Halla el área de cada rectángulo con largo × ancho, y observa que las dos piezas están una al lado de la otra, sin traslaparse.
Primer rectángulo: 9 × 6 = 54 sq ft. Ahora halla el área del segundo rectángulo y combínala con la primera.

level3.stem: Plan 4 — Design studio: the floor is a 16 ft by 12 ft rectangle, but a 5 ft by 4 ft storage closet is cut out of one corner. Find the usable floor area.
level3.explanation: Large rectangle = 16 x 12 = 192 sq ft. Cutout closet = 5 x 4 = 20 sq ft. A piece is removed, so subtract: 192 - 20 = 172 sq ft.
choiceFeedback: That's the full floor — subtract the closet that's cut out.
You added the closet — it's removed, so subtract its area.
20 is just the closet — subtract it from the whole floor.
level3.stemEs: Plan 4 — Estudio de diseño: el piso es un rectángulo de 16 ft por 12 ft, pero se recorta un clóset de almacenamiento de 5 ft por 4 ft en una esquina. Halla el área útil del piso.
level3.explanationEs: Rectángulo grande = 16 x 12 = 192 sq ft. Clóset recortado = 5 x 4 = 20 sq ft. Se quita una pieza, así que resta: 192 - 20 = 172 sq ft.
hints: The closet is removed from the floor, so that corner is not usable space.
Find the area of the whole rectangle first, then the area of the cutout, and decide which operation takes one away from the other.
Whole floor: 16 × 12 = 192 sq ft. The closet covers 5 × 4 sq ft — take that piece away to finish.
hintsEs: El clóset se quita del piso, así que esa esquina no es espacio útil.
Halla primero el área del rectángulo completo, luego el área del recorte, y decide qué operación quita una de la otra.
Piso completo: 16 × 12 = 192 sq ft. El clóset cubre 5 × 4 sq ft: quita esa pieza para terminar.

level3.stem: An L-shaped room is made of two rectangles: 10 ft × 6 ft and 4 ft × 3 ft. What is the total area?
level3.explanation: Area 1 = 10 × 6 = 60 sq ft. Area 2 = 4 × 3 = 12 sq ft. Total = 60 + 12 = 72 sq ft.
choiceFeedback: Double one side: area doubles.
Double both sides: area × 4.
hints: The L-shape is already split into two rectangles for you: 10 × 6 and 4 × 3.
Find each rectangle's area separately with A = l × w, then combine — joined shapes mean adding.
Compute 10 × 6 and 4 × 3, then add the two results. Label your answer in sq ft.
level3.stemEs: Una habitación en forma de L está formada por dos rectángulos: 10 ft × 6 ft y 4 ft × 3 ft. ¿Cuál es el área total?
level3.explanationEs: Área 1 = 10 × 6 = 60 sq ft. Área 2 = 4 × 3 = 12 sq ft. Total = 60 + 12 = 72 sq ft.
hintsEs: La figura en L ya está dividida en dos rectángulos por ti: 10 × 6 y 4 × 3.
Halla el área de cada rectángulo por separado con A = l × a y luego combínalas: figuras unidas significan sumar.
Calcula 10 × 6 y 4 × 3, y luego suma los dos resultados. Etiqueta tu respuesta en pies².

level3.stem: A rectangular patio is 15 ft × 10 ft with a 5 ft × 4 ft rectangular flower bed cut out. What is the remaining area?
level3.explanation: Patio = 15 × 10 = 150 sq ft. Cutout = 5 × 4 = 20 sq ft. Remaining = 150 − 20 = 130 sq ft.
choiceFeedback: Test: same perimeter, different areas?
A thin rectangle and a square can differ.
Perimeter does not determine area.
hints: The flower bed is CUT OUT of the patio — that phrase tells you which operation to use.
Find the full patio area (15 × 10) and the cutout area (5 × 4), then remove the cutout.
Compute 15 × 10 and 5 × 4, then subtract the flower bed's area from the patio's area.
level3.stemEs: Un patio rectangular mide 15 ft × 10 ft y tiene recortado un jardín rectangular de 5 ft × 4 ft. ¿Cuál es el área restante?
level3.explanationEs: Patio = 15 × 10 = 150 sq ft. Recorte = 5 × 4 = 20 sq ft. Área restante = 150 − 20 = 130 sq ft.
hintsEs: El jardín está RECORTADO del patio: esa frase te dice qué operación usar.
Halla el área total del patio (15 × 10) y el área del recorte (5 × 4), y luego quita el recorte.
Calcula 15 × 10 y 5 × 4, y luego resta el área del jardín del área del patio.

level3.stem: Find the area of an L-shape made of a 5×3 rectangle and a 2×4 rectangle.
choiceFeedback: Area and perimeter are not linked.
A thin shape can have big perimeter, small area.
You must use both to describe a shape.
hints: Two rectangles make this L: one is 5 × 3 and the other is 2 × 4.
Joined pieces mean you add their areas after computing each one with length × width.
Find 5 × 3, then 2 × 4, and add the two products together.
level3.stemEs: Halla el área de una figura en forma de L formada por un rectángulo de 5×3 y uno de 2×4.
hintsEs: Dos rectángulos forman esta L: uno es 5 × 3 y el otro es 2 × 4.
Las piezas unidas significan que sumas sus áreas después de calcular cada una con largo × ancho.
Halla 5 × 3, luego 2 × 4, y suma los dos productos.
